requirements.note: Plain list of all 160 rows. Each row has a category SF Symbol, the title in bold, and 'Category · time · ★ rating' below; times read as '1 hr 5 min'.

A horizontal row of chips: All plus all nine categories. Search covers titles and ingredients and combines with the category (Desserts + 'butter' gives 8 rows, each marked 'Contains butter'). The empty result is a ContentUnavailableView-style 'No Recipes Found' that names the category and the query.
The sort button opens a menu (Name A to Z / Time, quickest first / Rating, highest first) with a checkmark and icons. All three sort correctly, and the choice survives relaunch.

Header card shows category, a large title, and time/servings/rating with icons. A grouped stepper scales the amounts with tidy fractions (4½ tsp, ⅔, 1⅓) and shows a 'scaled from the original 6-serving' footer and a Reset button. Decrement is disabled at 1. Steps are numbered with filled number circles.
The heart in the nav bar toggles and fills red. The Favorites tab lists saved recipes, has a 'Remove' swipe action, and shows a helpful empty state with a 'Browse Recipes' button.
A favorite was still there after relaunch.

tells: The category filter is hand-made capsule chips in a horizontal scroller, where iOS would more often use a menu or segmented picker. They are well made, though.
Gram amounts scale as decimals (1.5 g, 0.3 g) while other units use fractions. This looks deliberate but is mixed.
The swiped row keeps a grey highlight behind the Remove action.
A.scroll: Smooth and native. No blank or popping rows when flung. The search bar stays pinned as the large title collapses. Scroll position is kept after pushing a recipe and coming back. Fling back to the top and pull past the top behave normally.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped list of all 160 rows: title, 'Category · time', and an orange star rating on the trailing side. A section header reads 'All · 160 recipes by name'.

A Category menu in the toolbar offers All Recipes plus nine categories. Search covers titles and ingredients and combines with the category (Desserts + 'butter' gives 8). The empty state has a 'Show All Recipes' button. The list doesn't say why a recipe matched an ingredient search.
A sort menu with name, time and rating. All three sort correctly, the button's label shows the current sort, and the choice survives relaunch.

A settings-style grouped form: Category, Time, Rating, Servings. The servings stepper also has an editable number field (number pad with a Done key; out-of-range input is clamped to 99). Scaling is correct with fractions. Decrement is disabled at 1. Steps are numbered with plain grey digits.
The heart toggles. The Favorites tab shows a count header and a 'Delete' swipe action. The empty state is helpful and has a 'Browse Recipes' button.
A favorite was still there after relaunch.

bugs: At the largest text size, list titles break inside a word with no hyphen ('Muffin' / 's').
At the largest text size on the recipe screen, the Rating row's value runs into the Servings row below it, and the stepper shrinks to a tiny control under the label.
tells: The empty-state titles ('No Recipes Found', 'No Favorites Yet') are regular weight, not the bold ContentUnavailableView title.
The accent colour is inconsistent: the tab bar and cursor are system blue, but the stars are orange.
Rows are tall (78 pt) for two lines of text.
The keyboard stays on Shift (capitals) while typing in the search field.
The recipe screen is a plain settings-style form with no prominent title; the name appears only in the small inline nav title.
The swipe action is labelled 'Delete' for un-favoriting, which isn't quite the right word.
B.scroll: Smooth. No blank or popping rows when flung, and scroll position is kept on returning from a recipe. Fling to the top and pull past the top behave natively.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and scroll natively. A is more finished: a real recipe header card, numbered step circles, proper bold empty states, ingredient-match hints in search results, and a clean layout at the largest text size. B breaks words mid-word and crowds the recipe rows at the largest size, and its accent colours, empty-state type and form-style detail screen read as less carefully made.
